title: Exact localization of fixed tensor and its normalized resolving comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], homotopy category $K(R)$ and unbounded derived localization $Q_h:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the triangulated structure of $K(R)$ and the exact functor $Q_h$ of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Use the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the resolving full subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of flat-term K-flat complexes, and the published bifunctor $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ with its specified natural comparison $c_{P,S}:Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R S)\cong T(Q_hP,Q_hS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Fix a K-flat complex $A$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Assume the fixed tensor operations $H_A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ and $H^A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R A)$ induce additive exact functors on $K(R)$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], invert quasi-isomorphisms after applying $Q_h$, and use the coherent signed shift maps $s^2_n,s^1_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts].
There exist additive exact functors $G_A,G^A:D(R)\to D(R)$ and natural isomorphisms $\eta_L:Q_hH_A\cong G_AQ_h$ and $\eta_R:Q_hH^A\cong G^AQ_h$. Their coherent integer-shift comparisons are the unique ones for which $\eta_L,\eta_R$ commute with shifts and restrict to $Q_hs^2_n,Q_hs^1_n$, with the canonical shift comparisons of $Q_h$ inserted. The functors carry every distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle with its connecting arrow.
There are unique natural isomorphisms $d_L:G_A\cong T(Q_hA,-)$ and $d_R:G^A\cong T(-,Q_hA)$ for which $(d_L)_{Q_hP}(\eta_L)_P=c_{A,P}$ and $(d_R)_{Q_hP}(\eta_R)_P=c_{P,A}$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_R$. If $r:P\to B$ is any quasi-isomorphism with $P\in\mathcal P_R$, the composite comparisons $e_L=(d_LQ_h)\eta_L$ and $e_R=(d_RQ_h)\eta_R$ have components
$$e_{L,B}=T(1,Q_hr)c_{A,P}(Q_hH_A(r))^{-1},\qquad e_{R,B}=T(Q_hr,1)c_{P,A}(Q_hH^A(r))^{-1}.$$
These formulas are independent of $r$ and are natural for every derived varying-argument map through $d_L,d_R$. The factorization with its signed shifts and normalized comparisons is unique up to its unique compatible natural isomorphism. No boundedness or flatness of cohomology is required.
